title: Investigate and hotfix multi-tenant token backpressure causing TTFT regressions
creator: Kenji Yamamoto
description:
Summary: Production alerts starting 2026-03-10 02:00 UTC reported abrupt TTFT regressions and token/sec drops for multiple hosted customers and several Dedicated clusters. Private (on-prem) customers running runtime-1.20 were not affected. Initial triage indicated a recent KV-cache eviction heuristic change deployed in runtime-1.22 that interacted poorly with the continuous-batching path under multi-tenant load, causing per-request backpressure and uneven token generation rates.

Impact: Intermittent 2–6x increase in time-to-first-token (TTFT) for affected requests and reduced sustained tokens/sec on 4 hosted customers (support tickets #5241, #5248, #5253) and 2 dedicated tenants. Some customer flows timed out and triggered retries, amplifying load.

Goal: Ship a targeted hotfix that (1) restores previous KV-cache behavior for multi-tenant pooling while preserving memory bounds, (2) removes the pathological interaction with batching, and (3) deploys mitigations and monitoring to prevent recurrence.
activity: 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC - Pager triggered by s3-latency alert; SREs paged; initial hypothesis: new eviction heuristic causing cache churn
2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - Reproduced locally with synthetic multi-tenant workload: observed frequent KV cache evictions when sequence length distribution changed, increased batching stalls
2026-03-10 06:20 UTC - Rollback of runtime-1.22 on one canary host reduced TTFT; confirmed correlation between heuristic and regression
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Engineering decision: implement fast hotfix (patch A) to add soft-guard for eviction under high concurrent KV reads rather than full rollback
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - Patch A implemented: introduce a per-shard read-lock window that delays eviction during active prefix reuse; unit + integration tests added
2026-03-11 01:00 UTC - Canary rollout of Patch A across 10% of hosted fleet; monitor dashboards show TTFT improvement on canaries; tokens/sec recovery observed
2026-03-11 08:45 UTC - Extended rollout to Dedicated staging clusters; one dedicated tenant reported residual jitter, added telemetry to inspect sequence-length edge cases
2026-03-11 14:00 UTC - Patch B (follow-up): adjust batching scheduler to prefer draining partially-full batches when KV cache miss rate spikes; reduces head-of-line blocking
2026-03-12 02:30 UTC - Integration test flake discovered in long-running sequence tests; fixed race in batch scheduler metrics; re-ran canaries

2026-03-12 10:15 UTC - Post-deploy monitoring: hosted customers impacted show median TTFT back within 1.1x baseline and tokens/sec within 95% of normal; notify customers and close escalations after confirmation
postmortem_actions: Add KV-cache heuristic unit tests covering multi-tenant concurrency and varying sequence-length histograms
Add an automated canary checklist for eviction-related kernel changes
Create an SLO-focused alert that correlates TTFT spikes with KV miss/eviction rates
Plan: runtime-1.22.1 to include hardened eviction algorithm and batching scheduler instrumentation
